html:
The Mazatec are an Indigenous people of the Sierra Mazateca in northern Oaxaca, Mexico, with smaller groups in Puebla and Veracruz. They speak Mazatec, an Oto-Manguean language; Ha Shuta Enima is their own name for themselves.

Mazatec is a tonal language, and in some villages people can hold whole conversations by whistling its tones. The Aztecs conquered the area in the 1400s, and the Spanish in the 1520s. The town of Huautla de Jiménez became world famous in 1957, when the healer María Sabina showed visitors her night ceremonies with psilocybin mushrooms, which were then described in Life magazine. In the 1950s the Miguel Alemán dam flooded part of their lowlands and moved thousands of people. See Mexico.
